video_title: Micah Nori Postgame Interview | Portland Trail Blazers 116, San Antonio Spurs 111 | Nov. 25, 2026

quotes.speaker: Micah Nori
quotes.summary_phrase: Micah Nori on team's commitment to player development and simplicity
quotes.excerpt: We don't need home runs, we just need more singles and just make the easy play.
quotes.quote: I think that we always talk about, and Gill and his staff in player development do a really good job about talking about pictures, just keeping it simple and all the short-sided games and all the CLA stuff and putting them in position and then just seeing what you see. The thing we talked about with these guys tonight was, we don't need home runs, we just need more singles and just make the easy play. Just get yourself downhill. If Victor Wembanyama presents himself early, kick it to the corner, which we did a phenomenal job of. We get up 53s, we make 19 of them, and we end up with 28 assists all the while shooting 31 free throws.
quotes.social_post: Micah Nori on the Blazers offensive strategy against the Spurs: We don't need home runs, we just need more singles and just make the easy play.

structured.context: Micah Nori discusses the team's offensive strategy of kicking the ball out when Victor Wembanyama presents himself in the paint.

quotes.speaker: Micah Nori
quotes.summary_phrase: Micah Nori on team's emotional composure and execution in clutch moments
quotes.excerpt: We talked about playing with emotion, but don't play emotional.
quotes.quote: We talked about it. This team, and good for them, they ended both of our seasons last year, meaning the Trail Blazers and my season, and then they embarrassed us last time they were here. So we talked about playing with emotion, but don't play emotional. When Victor Wembanyama got the big one, he was super excited, but we kept our composure. Then we come down and Drew made big threes all night. Whenever we needed one, he just seemed to hit a big one. And then Dame, he hit that one and then he hit the one coming out of the timeout that was huge.
quotes.social_post: Micah Nori on the Blazers composure in the clutch: We talked about playing with emotion, but don't play emotional.

structured.context: Micah Nori reflects on the team maintaining composure during a high-stakes game against the Spurs.

quotes.speaker: Micah Nori
quotes.summary_phrase: Micah Nori on Damian Lillard's defensive impact and effort
quotes.excerpt: I just thought he competed his butt off, got into the ball, did a really good job.
quotes.quote: Somebody posted something and he sent it to us on some tweet. I don't know what the number meant, the negative whatever, but all I know is it said, Wembanyama, Thompson, Dame Lillard, really Rudy Gobert. I didn't know we'd be talking about Dame Lillard for defensive player of the year, but I just thought he competed his butt off, got into the ball, did a really good job on a couple of isolations even versus Castle and all that. And he has really made it a point to not be, quote unquote, to be that guy. And he has been phenomenal as far as with his defensive effort.
quotes.social_post: Micah Nori on Damian Lillard's defensive effort: I didn't know we'd be talking about Dame Lillard for defensive player of the year, but I just thought he competed his butt off.

structured.context: Micah Nori praises Damian Lillard for his defensive effort and commitment to the team's defensive identity.

quotes.speaker: Micah Nori
quotes.summary_phrase: Micah Nori on team's strategic approach to shooting against San Antonio
quotes.excerpt: We weren't necessarily making it a point of emphasis to shoot up to shoot 53s.
quotes.quote: We weren't necessarily making it a point of emphasis to shoot up to shoot 53s. What we made a point of emphasis was with if you see Victor Wembanyama in the paint and you don't have a straight line to finish, to find the kickout and make the right play. They do a really good job because what they try to do, like a lot of teams, and we do the same things, try to play everything two-on-two, funnel it down to Victor Wembanyama and then stay home on shooters and then make you have to take mid-range and bad shots over top of Victor Wembanyama. But what happened was we were able to break down their initial pressure, not always with a pick-and-roll, and then Victor Wembanyama had to come over and help and then we were able and which chain reaction started opening up some things.
quotes.social_post: Micah Nori explains how the Blazers broke down the Spurs defense: We were able to break down their initial pressure and then Victor Wembanyama had to come over and help.

structured.context: Micah Nori explains how the team's ball movement successfully countered the Spurs' defensive funneling toward Victor Wembanyama.

quotes.speaker: Micah Nori
quotes.summary_phrase: Micah Nori on the team's belief in their collective potential
quotes.excerpt: I do believe in that group and that locker room. I said that more for them than anybody.
quotes.quote: I do believe in that group and that locker room. I said that more for them than anybody, that expect to win. We don't win by happenstance. We win because we are a top-10 defensive team and we're a top-10 offensive team and it doesn't matter that we've had some injuries. Everybody's had injuries. And even you could say we've won some games that maybe if everybody was healthy we may not have, but I just honestly believe because the way our depth is, the way our pieces work, the leadership that we have, the way the guys go about their business, my job is very, very easy because I never have to coach effort. All we have to do is put these guys in the right spots. There's tremendous amount of buying, they all winning is the most important thing.
quotes.social_post: Micah Nori on his team's culture: My job is very, very easy because I never have to coach effort. There is a tremendous amount of buying, they all winning is the most important thing.

structured.context: Micah Nori discusses the team's resilience and depth despite dealing with various injuries throughout the season.

quotes.speaker: Micah Nori
quotes.summary_phrase: Micah Nori on the challenge of defending Victor Wembanyama
quotes.excerpt: When you have no fear that anyone can block your shot, that's a compliment to him.
quotes.quote: 44 points, but I guess if the man, oh man, he's a problem. You know, Dwayne Casey used to always talk about Kevin Durant, meaning the rim is always open because he's seven-foot and the way he shoots the ball. It's the same thing for Victor Wembanyama. Like when you have no fear that anyone can block your shot, and that's not a detriment to him, that's a compliment to him, and he just got himself to his spots, he found in rhythm. All we tried to do is make it difficult and I mean he goes 17 for 33, 9 for 9 from three. He made some tough ones. When you go 14 for 21 on twos, I don't know what he was at the rim, and then you give him 10 free throws, I just he is an absolute problem.
quotes.social_post: Micah Nori on Victor Wembanyama after his 44 point performance: He is an absolute problem.

structured.context: Micah Nori describes the difficulty of defending Victor Wembanyama after the player scored 44 points in the game.
